notes: A caller-class-sensitive operation (GetPermissionUsedRecordsAsync) runs behind a caller permission check and no named caller-role predicate. The permission fact is honest and insufficient: a permission is not a caller class, so the boundary the rule asks about is exactly the one that is absent.

caller_class_positive plus one line: a named caller-role predicate (IPCSkeleton::IsSystemAppCalling) rejects callers outside the class before the operation. The pair differs in exactly that line, so the suppressed candidate is attributable to the caller-class fact and not to a widened guard set.

A look-alike permission-usage query (GetPermissionUsageSummary) at the same site. The rule is scoped to a reviewed set of names rather than to a call shape, so a sibling API that is not on that set raises nothing.

AccessTokenKit::VerifyAccessToken is a reviewed result-domain predicate; it is called with the calling UID where its result domain is a caller TokenID. The same call also loses its permission credit -- the submitted identity is a different domain, so the guarded operation is recorded as unguarded as well as mis-domained. That coupling is the rule's point and is why this positive carries three candidates.
identity_domain_positive with the submitted identity changed from IPCSkeleton::GetCallingUid() to IPCSkeleton::GetCallingTokenID() -- the remediation the rule names, and no other line changes.
request_identity_positive with the principal changed from a Parcel-supplied token to the IPC caller TokenID; the candidate rule must be suppressed.
